text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - Bunds and futures slipped down in late European trade, unwilling to make a convincing break higher while U.S. Treausuries remained soft. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.60, down 0.21 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilt futures slid around half a point in the last half-hour of trade after a French opinion poll showed the centre-right coalition with only a wafer-thin lead over the opposition Socialists. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-02/32, down 14/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond and interest rate futures came under pressure as an opinion poll suggesting the ruling coalition would win only a slim majority unsettled an already nervous marketplace. The June bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.62, up 0/02 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Bond futures ended lower in line with many other European bond markets and cautious ahead of a long weekend in Italy with markets here closed on Friday for Liberation Day. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 126.93, down 0.59 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were moderately lower at midday, weighed down by a slew of both Treasury and corporate supply this week. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 107-11/32, down 12/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.12 percent.

JAPAN - The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended slightly higher after paring some gains toward the close on Thursday. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 126.56, down 0.19 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The Eurobond market was sluggish, although a handful of significant mainstream deals were launched. Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) brought a $500 million five-year Eurobond, its largest bond issue to date. The deal was priced to yield nine basis points over U.S. Treasuries and traded in to six b.p. over by 1200 GMT.
